clue.text: Mike's dismissed by someone spouting here?

definitions.text: Mike's dismissed by someone spouting here?

parts.words: Mike's dismissed by someone spouting here?
parts.note: a place where orators address the crowd with their own lungs, scorning a microphone (mike), as on the famous soapbox spot in Hyde Park

explanation.surface: A soapbox orator waves away the offer of a microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike is a casual word for a microphone; the Hyde Park spot for public ranting is known for unamplified voices on soapboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-east corner of Hyde Park in London is the traditional open-air venue for anyone wishing to harangue passers-by.

clue.text: Flag, having to bear leaderless team's burden

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it

indicators.note: a team losing its leader drops its opening letter

parts.note: a team is a crew, so team's gives crew's, the apostrophe ignored
a cross to bear is a burden

explanation.surface: A flag-bearer is weighed down carrying the load for a team with no captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' removes the C from CREWS, leaving REWS. The answer is the white saltire on blue, the flag of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The saltire of Scotland's patron saint is the national flag of Scotland.

clue.text: Dead men found in drains

definitions.meaning: dead men is slang for empty bottles after drinking
drains as a verb: pours out the contents of, leaves with nothing inside

explanation.walkthrough: Dead men here are not corpses but finished bottles left on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty bottles are jokingly called dead men, and to drain a vessel is to leave it with nothing in it.

clue.text: Snake artist portrayed in clothes

indicators.note: the artist is shown wearing the clothes, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: kit is a set of clothes, as in football kit
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter is depicted in some outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The krait is a venomous South Asian snake related to cobras.

clue.text: Reserved appeal upheld in late case

indicators.note: the appeal sits within the other word, which serves as its case
the late word forms a case around the turned appeal

parts.note: late in the sense of recent, not long past

indicators.note: in a down clue upheld means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: IT is sex appeal, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: A judge upholds an appeal in a recent court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' gives TI, read upwards as in a down clue; 'in' and 'case' make the late word wrap it. IT for sex appeal is an old convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is quiet and holds back, which is what being uncommunicative means.

clue.text: Programmer brings in good old chap

indicators.note: the programmer takes another letter inside himself

parts.note: a coder is someone who writes programs

explanation.surface: A software developer introduces a nice elderly gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A codger is an informal word for an elderly man, often a slightly eccentric one.

clue.text: Entrance for office party

definitions.meaning: the front area of a building where visitors arrive and are greeted
a formal party or function, such as one held at work

explanation.definitionFit: The desk area where guests arrive and a formal welcome gathering both share the same word.

clue.text: Subterfuge picked up rumour about tax cut

indicators.note: the turned rumour goes around the shortened tax
in a down clue picked up means the word is lifted, so read upwards

parts.note: noise in the sense of talk or report going about

indicators.note: cut means the tax loses its final letter

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: Gossip about trimming taxes is being spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' gives ESION, the rumour read upwards; 'cut' docks the tax; 'about' wraps ESION round it. 'Picked up' tempts as a homophone signal, but this is a down clue reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging a question or obligation by trickery is a form of subterfuge.

clue.text: Lenin turned out to keep study in main street of capital

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold another piece inside them
out signals the letters are put out of order

parts.note: a den is a private room for working, a study

explanation.surface: Lenin is ejected so as to keep a study going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles the dictator's name with 'turned'; 'to keep' sets the study inside. 'turned' tempts as the anagram signal, yet its letters are needed. The answer is Berlin's grand avenue, Under the Lime Trees.
explanation.definitionFit: This lime-tree-lined boulevard is the grand central avenue of Berlin, Germany's capital.

clue.text: Left in death throes by poisoner, given some black stuff

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, the poisoner of Cleopatra

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the jumbled word
throes are convulsions, so the word is thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone left dying by a poisoner was given some black stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throes' shuffles death to HATED; 'in' slots the L inside it. Cleopatra's asp is the poisoner, and the black stuff is road tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the black tarry surfacing material, so a road given it has been surfaced.

clue.text: Wickets so far apart in cricket series

definitions.text: Wickets so far apart in cricket
definitions.meaning: the old unit of 22 yards is the distance between the two sets of stumps on a cricket pitch
a connected sequence of things or events

explanation.walkthrough: The 22-yard length of a cricket pitch, wicket to wicket, equals one old surveyor's unit of measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A linked sequence is called by the same name as the 22-yard measure equal to a cricket pitch's length.

clue.text: Meaning to go with the tide

definitions.meaning: the gist or general sense of what is said
to float along carried by the current

explanation.definitionFit: The gist of an argument and floating passively along with a current share one word.

clue.text: Vulgar arrogance is one of the ways of the City

definitions.text: one of the ways of the City

parts.note: cheap in the sense of tawdry or vulgar
side is old slang for swagger or pretentiousness

explanation.surface: Coarse conceit is said to be a hallmark of City folk.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAPSIDE is a historic street in the City of London, the financial district; ways means streets.
explanation.definitionFit: This old market street is one of the thoroughfares of the City of London, the square mile.

clue.text: The rest paid any number let in given right of passage

parts.note: ease is rest or relaxation

indicators.note: the number is admitted inside the word for paid

parts.note: met as in met the bill, paid it
N stands for an indefinite number in maths

explanation.surface: The rest of the fee was paid once a number of people were admitted with access granted.
explanation.walkthrough: An EASEMENT is a legal right over another's land, such as a right of way; the clue plays on rite of passage.
explanation.definitionFit: In property law this is a right to use another person's land, typically to cross it.

clue.text: Illuminating reflections on Beethoven's work

definitions.meaning: light bounced off the lunar surface that lights up the night
the popular nickname of his Piano Sonata No 14

explanation.definitionFit: Night light reflected off the lunar surface also names Beethoven's famous piano sonata.

clue.text: Made one's name as a writer

definitions.text: Made one's name as a writer

parts.words: Made one's name as a writer
parts.note: read not as becoming famous but as literally writing your own name on a document

explanation.walkthrough: 'Made one's name' suggests winning fame as an author; it means putting a signature on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing one's name on a document is to put one's signature on it.

clue.text: Old animal I used in beef dish

parts.note: past means bygone, old
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An aged creature is used in a beef recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked cured beef, often served in sandwiches.

clue.text: Area for military escort to fall out

indicators.note: falling out on parade means breaking ranks, so the letters scatter

explanation.surface: A zone where a military escort is ordered to fall out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a defined zone of operations allotted to a military unit.

clue.text: Fancy headgear, right to overcome formality

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit over the next one

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
ice is cold formality or reserve, as in break the ice

explanation.surface: A fancy hat lets the wearer overcome stuffy formality.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a sudden whim, and a fancy is the same sort of passing desire.

clue.text: Assert cockfight isn't commonly held

indicators.note: the colloquial word is held inside the cockfight word

parts.note: a main is an old term for a cockfighting match
ain't is the common or nonstandard form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone claims that a cockfight is not normally staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' sets the slang inside the cockfight word, splitting it after its first letter. A main is a dated word for a cockfighting match.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a view is to assert it firmly against opposition.

clue.text: A paper hanky, some say, needed after this?

definitions.text: A paper hanky, some say, needed after this?

indicators.note: some say signals that the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: a tissue is a paper handkerchief

explanation.surface: A tissue is wanted after a sneeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a tissue' resembles the sound of a sneeze, after which you reach for one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the written form of the noise of sneezing, after which a hanky is wanted.

clue.text: Dry month, following one the. 'same except for the middle

indicators.note: the month comes after the shortened copy
the middle two letters of the word are taken away

parts.note: the same month as the one just named
June is a month

explanation.surface: A dry month follows another one just like it, except in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for the middle' leaves JE from a second copy of the month; 'following' puts the month after. The page's stray punctuation after 'the' is an OCR artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune means dull and insipid, and dry describes such lifeless writing.

clue.text: Hideous victim of disease sent back fast

indicators.note: sending the word back means reading its letters in reverse

parts.note: a leper suffers from leprosy
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: An ugly sufferer of illness was quickly sent home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent is revolting to look at, just as hideous things are.

clue.text: Into the world I brought one antelope

indicators.note: the letter goes into the world word

parts.note: an orb is a globe or the world
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: I brought a child into the world, plus an antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope of grasslands.

clue.text: Make speech from floor, at EGM

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within these consecutive letters

explanation.surface: A shareholder speaks from the floor at an extraordinary general meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, often pompously.

clue.text: Change opinion of jazz

definitions.meaning: a style of big-band jazz of the 1930s and 40s

explanation.definitionFit: A shift in voting intention and a big-band jazz style share one word.

clue.text: Not embarrassed by nude dancing, holding a party

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the other pieces inside them
dancing letters move about into a new order

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: Someone is unfazed by a naked dancer at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' shuffles the naked word to UNED; 'holding' wraps it round the party. 'by nude dancing' paints a scene but is pure mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabashed means without any shame or self-consciousness.

clue.text: Disappoint colleague prepared to unload lorry, perhaps

definitions.meaning: dropped the hinged flap of a truck so goods can be taken off

explanation.definitionFit: Failing your team and lowering a truck's tailboard flap use the same phrase.
